narrative.northStar: The Code Editor with a Chat Panel
narrative.overview:
The interface reads as a code editor that grew a chat panel. The portfolio's home page is the cover sheet; /chat is the workbench; the source code is the receipt. Every surface is dual-purpose: it has to communicate competence to a portfolio visitor in under a minute, and it has to disappear into a long developer session in /chat.

The system is sharp, technical, AI-native. Personality over decoration. Density over breathing room. One accent (Bio Emerald) used surgically, never as wallpaper. The interface is fluent in the category's best tools (Linear, Vercel, Raycast, Replit) and would never make a developer stop to wonder what an affordance does.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default. Single dark theme; light mode is wired but unused.
Tonal layering (background -> card -> popover -> secondary) carries hierarchy; shadows are reserved for state.
One saturated color, used for selection, primary action, and current state only.
Monospace (Geist Mono) for code, prompts, timestamps, file names, technical labels - not for body.
Type and motion are quiet. The user does the work; the interface does not perform.

rules.name: The Bio Emerald Rule
rules.body: The primary accent is used on <=10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. The accent is reserved for selection, primary action, current state, and the focused-input border. It does not glow, does not gradient, and does not appear as decoration.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow with a saturated color. No filter: drop-shadow() on the emerald. The accent communicates through presence, not through radiance.

rules.name: The Tonal Layering Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is conveyed by surface tone, not by shadow. Background -> Card -> Popover -> Secondary -> Accent is a five-step ramp; each step is <=5% lightness apart.

rules.name: The Mono is a Tool Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for code, prompts, timestamps, file names, version metadata, and the footer attribution. It is not the body font.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Budget Rule
rules.body: One eyebrow per page. A section can use an eyebrow as a deliberate brand system; two or more in close vertical proximity becomes the AI scaffold reflex and stops reading as voice.

rules.name: The Geist Pairing Rule
rules.body: Geist Sans carries all UI text. Geist Mono carries code, prompts, timestamps, file names, technical labels, and the footer attribution. The pair is neutral and technical; the personality comes from copy and layout, not from the type. Don't add a third sans to the system.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A card sits on the surface by being a different tone, not by being lifted by a shadow. Shadows appear only on buttons, focused inputs, and the chat input at rest.

rules.name: The No-Stacking Rule
rules.body: No card stacks on a card. A list of cards on a tonal surface is fine; a card-within-a-card is not.

rules.name: The Chat Bubble Rule
rules.body: Both bubbles use Geist Sans (never font-serif), a single tonal surface per role (assistant = bg-secondary, user = bg-primary/10 + border), and a rounded-2xl geometry. No gradient, no glass, no shadow, no role-asymmetric typography. The asymmetry is tone and alignment only.

rules.name: The Empty-State Heading Rule
rules.body: Tool empty states (chat, search, settings) use the Headline role (text-lg font-semibold), not the Display h1. The Display h1 is a one-per-page budget reserved for the hero.

rules.name: The Resume Sandbox Rule
rules.body: The resume in /chat is a per-conversation sandbox of sections, not a single streamed object. Each recruiter prompt emits a patch (add/update/remove/reorder) that the client merges into the sandbox; the right panel renders the merged view. The sandbox persists across turns in localStorage keyed by conversation id. The chat's diff card surfaces the orchestration: Added N, Updated M, Removed K, Reordered R. The model never wipes the resume.

dos: Do use Bio Emerald for selection, primary action, current state, and the focused-input border only.
Do use the surface ramp (base -> card -> popover -> secondary -> accent) to convey hierarchy before reaching for shadow or weight.
Do pair Geist Sans with Geist Mono on code, prompts, timestamps, file names, and the footer attribution.
Do keep button radius consistent at rounded-md (10px) - except the chat input's send button, which is rounded-xl (16px) to read as a primary affordance.
Do cap body line length at 75ch and use text-wrap: balance on the hero h1.
Do keep motion to state changes (150-250ms) and use cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) as the standard ease.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every animation.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color. The Bio Emerald carries selection; nothing else earns a saturated color.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts. Never intentional.
Don't apply background-clip: text to a gradient. Decorative, never meaningful. Use a single solid color.
Don't use glassmorphism as a default. Blurs and glass cards are decorative.

Don't ship animate-bounce on the scroll indicator (current state: components/landing/scroll-indicator.tsx:10). Replace with a subtle vertical translate using cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) and a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce fallback.
Don't put a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow above every section. One per page is the budget (see The Eyebrow Budget Rule). Two or more reads as the AI scaffold reflex.
Don't use 01 / 02 / 03 numbered markers as default scaffolding above sections. Numbered markers earn their place when the section is a real ordered sequence.

Don't default to Card for grouping. The portfolio widgets, the chat sidebar items, the starter chips, the dialog list items are all 'a piece of content on a surface' - they sit on the surface by tone, not by card-within-card.
Don't pair Geist Sans with another sans. The Geist Mono is the contrast pair; that's enough.
Don't use em dashes in copy. Use commas, colons, semicolons, periods, or parentheses.
Don't ship a label like 'Empower your AI journey' or 'Unlock the future of coding.' Specific nouns and verbs; the product is an open-source AI app builder, not a movement.
Don't add a second dark mode shade. The system is single-theme dark. Light mode is technically wired (next-themes) but unused; leave it dormant.
Don't wipe the resume on every prompt. The sandbox is the recruiter's working artifact; the agent patches it. See The Resume Sandbox Rule.
